builderInsights.title: Ryo Lu
builderInsights.suggestedTitle: AIでプロダクトを過剰に盛り込みやすくなりすぎた
builderInsights.suggestedSummary: 彼らは、多くのダメなプロダクトは1つの致命的な判断で壊れるのではないと言う。むしろ、誰も止めなかった妥当な追加が積み重なって崩れるのだ。AIでリリースコストがほぼゼロまで下がった今、チームは機能も概念も仕上げも際限なく足せる。結果として、より騒がしく、まとまりのないプロダクトになる。

tweets.text:
overcooking

you've seen this: someone ships a dashboard that shows every number with a sparkline, every action has a confirmation modal, every empty state has an animated illustration and a tagline. individually each decision made sense to someone. together it feels like chaos. nothing is in focus.

that's overcooking. not one bad decision in isolation, but the accumulation of reasonable ones that no one said no to.

AI makes this worse as the cost of adding dropped to near zero. it can build a feature, even a whole new concept in minutes. so people do. and then they do it again. the thing that started with a clear purpose slowly becomes a collection of additions that are each justifiable but collectively incoherent.

the root problem is that most "new ideas" aren't new. they're repackaging of something that already exists at a more fundamental level. a new sticker on an old concept. it feels like progress because something changed, with a new word and skin – but the thinking didn't go deeper, it just duplicated itself into confusion.

the whole has a core. you feel it once you understand the whole system. everything in it are related and balanced. when you overload it, that gravity weakens. not because any one thing is wrong – but because attention is finite and you force it everywhere.

what we need aren't more tools that make more slop. it's seeing through the chaos, and returning to what the thing actually is, and cutting everything that doesn't serve that. that's harder now, not easier. because there's always something else you could add with one more prompt.

This is probably the biggest news yet in software going headless, and will bring knowledge work agents to the masses. The new ChatGPT agents have access to any of the tools and data you want to work with, with complete coding and tool use available to them. 

Here's an example of a custom sales assistant agent uses Box as a knowledge source for accessing enterprise content securely to answer questions and generate new content on the fly. builderInsights.title: Guillermo Rauch
builderInsights.suggestedTitle: より広範な credential theft ring を追うペタバイト規模の捜査
builderInsights.suggestedSummary: 彼によれば、Vercel の security team はほぼ 1 ペタバイトの logs を掘り下げた。その結果、攻撃者は元の Context.ai 侵害に結びついていただけではなかった。各 provider をまたいで token と key を盗む malware をばらまいていたのだ。Vercel は現在、Microsoft、AWS、Wiz と連携している。他の被害者には creds のローテーションを促しつつ、product fixes のリリースを続けている。

tweets.text:
I want to keep everyone updated on the details of the security investigation.

The team performed an in-depth analysis to search for root causes and to better understand the behavior of the threat actor.

We cast a very wide net, pulling and processing nearly a petabyte of logs of the entire Vercel Network and API, extending well beyond the initial Context[.]ai compromise.

We now understand that the threat actor has been active beyond that startup's compromise. Threat intel points to the distribution of malware to computers in search of valuable tokens like keys to Vercel accounts and other providers.

Once the attacker gets ahold of those keys, our logs show a repeated pattern: rapid and comprehensive API usage, with a focus on enumeration of non-sensitive environment variables.

As a result:
◾We've deepened and widened our collaboration with partners across the industry, like Microsoft, AWS and Wiz, to further protect the broader internet.
◾ We've notified other suspected victims of this threat actor, independent of this event, encouraging them to rotate credentials and adopt best practices.

We've also shipped a bunch more product enhancements. I'm extremely thankful to our team and industry partners for working around the clock. For more details on the ongoing investigation, refer to our security bulletin:
https://t.co/BLVnic9fJC

builderInsights.title: Dan Shipper
builderInsights.suggestedTitle: AI仕事の端に人間が残る
builderInsights.suggestedSummary: 彼は、LLMはすでに大半のエンジニアより良いコードを書くと言う。だから人間の本当の仕事は、問題をどう切り出すかを決め、最後に出力を見極めることだ。Cora ComputerのKieran Klaassenとの対話では、「AI sandwich」発想を押し出す。モデルが中身を担い、人間は前後を挟み、compound engineeringでrepoに学習を蓄積していく。要するに、いつ介入し、いつagentに任せるかを知っていれば、1人のエンジニアでも小さなチーム並みにshipできるという話だ。

tweets.text:
YouTube: https://t.co/mxQBcSt014 

Spotify: https://t.co/GhHxzfZyaJ

LLMs write better code than most human engineers. If code is handled, what's left for us?

I chatted with @kieranklaassen, GM of @CoraComputerCora and creator of compound engineering, on @every's AI & I about where humans fit now that AI can generate high-quality code, copy, strategy, and design. His theory: We’re the bread.

Humans are indispensable at the beginning and end of every process. At the beginning, to set the frame, and at the end to provide the final polish.

This turned into a wide-ranging conversation on the future of humans and AI in coding and beyond.

We get into:
- Why AI work is a sandwich. The models are the filling, responsible for writing, testing, and iterating. Humans are the bread bookending the models: We frame the problem and judge whether the output feels right.
- The four steps behind compound engineering: Plan, work, review, and compound. The last one—where learnings feed back into the repo so agents don't repeat their mistakes—is what allows one engineer to ship like a team of five.
- Play to your strengths. Knowing when to step away and let the models execute lets you focus on areas that require human judgement, like approaching a problem from multiple angles.

This is a must-watch for anyone trying to figure out their role in the workplace now that the execution layer is largely solved.

podcastHighlights.title: AIサンドイッチ: AI時代に人間が強い領域
podcastHighlights.suggestedTitle: 人間は前後を担い、AIは中身を担うべきだ
podcastHighlights.suggestedSummary:
**要点:** 勝ち筋は完全自動化ではない。判断、センス、責任が重要な両端に人間を置くことだ。

**主な示唆**
- Compound EngineeringはAIの仕事をサンドイッチのように捉える。人間が枠組みを決め、agentが中身を進め、最後に人間が戻って判断し、磨き上げる。
- 人間の価値が最も高いのは、常時の監視ではない。AIが最も苦手とする2か所、つまり曖昧な問題設定と、最後のセンスに基づく仕上げだ。
- 単純作業の中身が自動化されるほど、仕事はプロダクト思考、マネジメント、そして個人的で、美しく、「自分のもの」と感じられるものを作る方向へ移る。

**ストーリー**
QuoraのGMであり、Every内で使われているCompound Engineeringフレームワークの生みの親でもあるKieranは、実務的な問いからこのアプローチを作った。どうすれば、人間らしさを失わせずにAIにもっと速く、もっと良い仕事をさせられるのか。彼の答えは、計画、実行、レビュー、そして学びをrepoに保存してagentが時間とともに改善する「compound」ステップを含むワークフローだ。

だが、より深い示唆は人間の居場所にある。初期段階では、アイデア出しと問題設定に人間が深く関わるべきだ。後半では、モデルに実行を任せる。そして最後に、センスを持って戻ってくる。彼の言葉を借りれば、「最初と最後は人間で、中身はかなりうまく自動化できる」。

だからこそ、常に人間が関与し続けるべきだという考えには彼は反論する。本当のレバレッジは、いつ深く考え、いつ手放すかを見極めることだ。彼はそれを音楽にたとえる。中身は練習だが、演奏の瞬間にこそ何か生きたものが立ち上がる。ソフトウェアでも、デザインでも、文章でも同じだ。成果物を本当に自分のものにしたいなら、完全に外注することはできない。基準は上がり続ける。だから人間の強みは、ただ作業をこなすことではなく、「気持ちいい」と感じられるものを作ることへ移っていく。
